meta.description: Sri Lanka Constitution — Chapter III (fundamental rights) excerpt. Keys are derived from article + clause unless `canonical_key` is set on a row.

clauses.text: Every person is entitled to freedom of thought, conscience and religion, including the freedom to have or to adopt a religion or belief of his choice.
No person shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.
All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.
No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.
It shall be lawful to require a person to acquire within a reasonable time sufficient knowledge of any language as a qualification for employment or office where necessary.
It shall be lawful to require sufficient knowledge of any language where duties cannot be performed otherwise.
No person shall be subject to any disability or restriction regarding access to public places on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste or sex.
Special provisions may be made for the advancement of women, children or disabled persons.
No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.
Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.
Any accused person has the right to a fair trial and legal representation.
Punishment can only be imposed by a competent court and detention before trial is not punishment.
Every person is presumed innocent until proven guilty.
The burden of proving certain facts may be placed on the accused by law.
No person shall be guilty of an offence that was not an offence at the time it was committed, nor receive a heavier penalty.
Acts considered criminal under general principles of international law can still be punished.
Minimum penalties may be imposed as long as they do not exceed the maximum at the time.
Detention under immigration or deportation laws shall not be considered a violation.
Freedom of speech and expression including publication.
Freedom of peaceful assembly.
Freedom of association.
Freedom to form and join a trade union.
Freedom to manifest religion or belief.
Freedom to enjoy and promote culture and language.
Freedom to engage in lawful occupation or business.
Freedom of movement and residence.
Freedom to return to Sri Lanka.
Certain long-term residents are entitled to these rights for ten years.
Every citizen has the right to access information held by public authorities and related institutions.
Restrictions on this right must be lawful and necessary in a democratic society.
Citizen includes bodies where at least three-fourths of members are citizens.
Certain rights may be restricted for national security.
Freedom of speech may be restricted for harmony, defamation, or incitement.
Freedom of assembly may be restricted for harmony.
Freedom of association may be restricted for harmony or economy.
Freedom of occupation may be restricted by qualifications or state control.
Freedom of movement may be restricted for national economy.
General restrictions may apply for national security, public order, health, morality, and welfare.
Additional restrictions apply to armed forces and police for discipline and duty.
Existing laws remain valid even if inconsistent with fundamental rights.
Punishments under existing law are not violations.
Every person has the right to apply to the Supreme Court for violations of fundamental rights.
